I lived in South Africa for quite some time and this whole "Fuck every racist" thing really annoys me because it seems to me that the people on here have this ideal that you can't have the notion of "black against white" without being racist. South Africa shows you can.

First of all, being racist is horrible and should be avoided at all cost.

Now, let us build some context. If you live in a country where the separation "Us against Them" is cultural and is everywhere and when the "us" is the black people and the "them" is everyone else racism becomes harder to define as a absolute concept. In South Africa if you are black and you defend a white man you become white in the eyes of everyone else but (and this is the important part) if you are white and defend black peoples rights you are still white and you have very few rights. So in most cases it is a war between two factions and people there don't see racism they see survival. And when you live in this environment it is hard not to see the rest of the world as having the same divisions. So, instead of regarding this as the "this is racist and doesn't deserve my attention" maybe we should try and see the context within which it was written and then analyse those opinions and form our conclusions. We may still be against some or most of them but I believe they deserve to be considered and analysed and not dismissed.

TL;DR; Just because you don't like someone's behavior it does not mean that all their opinions are worthless.
